summary: We developed MARSWalk, a Mars mission-planning prototype combining Perseverance and Curiosity rover locations, recorded routes, 3D terrain, distance measurements, and historical natural events on one layered map. It addresses the challenge by helping users explore destinations and compare potential routes using real Mars data. MARSWalk makes complex exploration records easier to understand, with traceable sources, clearly labeled data gaps, and transparent assumptions to support informed early mission planning.
details:
MARSWalk is an interactive Mars mission planning prototype that combines Perseverance and Curiosity rover data in one layered map It helps users explore rover locations recorded traverses terrain and historical natural events in Jezero and Gale craters

Users can select rover stations to view their recorded positions Martian sols photos and sources Recorded traverses show where the rovers drove while clearly labeled synthetic connectors distinguish gaps in the archive Within available terrain coverage a two point planner compares straight line distance with a slope aware route reporting distance ascent and estimated travel time based on labeled assumptions

The application offers a 2D map local 3D terrain and a rotatable Mars globe Elevation models support slope hillshade and contour layers alongside toggleable geology and imagery The globe provides planetary context and great circle distance measurements rather than detailed global routing A historical archive presents events such as dust storms marsquakes and meteoroid impacts by Earth date and Martian sol with location precision and uncertainty made explicit

MARSWalk makes exploration records easier to understand and compare for early mission planning Source based information traces to downloaded records missing data is marked unavailable and calculated estimates are separated from observations Future goals include live updates additional rovers and landing sites and improved interaction The prototype is not an operational navigation system or a validated human safety assessment

MARSWalk also includes a radiation panel showing historical surface measurements from the Curiosity RAD instrument in Gale crater during 2012 and 2013 sourced from Hassler et al 2014 These measurements cover galactic cosmic rays and exclude solar energetic particle events They provide historical context rather than current radiation forecasts or a safety assessment Measurements are not transferred to Jezero where the panel shows that radiation has not been computed

The software uses JavaScript and JSX React 19 and Vite Three js React Three Fiber and Drei for 3D Leaflet React Leaflet and proj4 for mapping GeoTIFF for terrain data and Vitest for tests Python and shell scripts support source retrieval and provenance verification
